source_evidence.observation: The one-dimensional source transform is a complex, unnormalized Fourier transform with kernel exp(i*2*pi*j*k/N), indices 0 through N-1, and complex input x(k).

The FFT is represented by a mixed-radix matrix factorization with permutation matrices P_l, Fourier blocks B_l of orders N_l, and M-1 diagonal twiddle-factor matrices D_l. The factorization covers Cooley-Tukey and Sande-Tukey algorithms with different D_l matrices.
The Wilkinson model is fl(a+b)=a(1+theta*epsilon)+b(1+theta*epsilon) and fl(ab)=ab(1+theta*epsilon), where each occurrence of theta may differ and satisfies -1 <= theta <= 1.

The paper introduces gamma >= 0 with fl(sin(fl(a)))=sin(a)+gamma*theta*epsilon and fl(cos(fl(a)))=cos(a)+gamma*theta*epsilon. Gamma depends on the computation of the functions and their arguments for a given transform order, but not on the input data.
For a one-dimensional FFT order N factored as N=N_1...N_M, K(N,gamma)=sum_{r=1}^M alpha(N_r)+(M-1)(3+2*gamma), where alpha(2)=sqrt(2), alpha(4)=5, and alpha(n)=2*sqrt(n)*(n+gamma) otherwise.
The multidimensional exact transform sums X(s_1,...,s_m) over every s_l=0,...,N_l-1 using the phase e(s_1*t_1/N_1+...+s_m*t_m/N_m), with every output index t_l in the same range.

The pointwise forward error is E(t)=fl(Y(t))-Y(t), its RMS is the square root of the average of |E(t)|^2 over all N_1...N_m entries, and Theorem 2(a) states [fl(Y)-Y]_RMS/Y_RMS <= epsilon*sum_{l=1}^m K(N_l,gamma)+O(epsilon^2).

conclusions: [Selected conclusion, Theorem 2(a)] [fl(Y)-Y]_RMS/Y_RMS <= epsilon*sum_{l=1}^m K(N_l,gamma)+O(epsilon^2). Evidence: PDF p. 8, printed p. 764, anchor "Theorem 2(a)".

statement.algorithm_linkage: The multidimensional computation is modeled as fl(T_1 fl(T_2 ... fl(T_m X))), so T_m is applied first and T_1 last; T_l is the one-dimensional Fourier transform in coordinate l, with Z_m=X, Z_0=Y, and Z_{l-1}=T_l Z_l. Each T_l must be a floating-point FFT to which Theorem 1's K applies. That K comes from the mixed-radix factorization (2.2), includes separate multiplications by the M_l-1 diagonal twiddle matrices, and is compatible with Cooley-Tukey or Sande-Tukey factorizations having different diagonal matrices. Evidence: PDF p. 8, printed p. 764, anchor "nested computation and rewriting of (4.1)"; PDF p. 2, printed p. 758, anchor "equation (2.2) and remarks following (2.2)"; PDF p. 3, printed p. 759, anchor "Theorem 1 and definition of K(N,gamma)".
numerical_model: [Explicit] fl(a+b)=a(1+theta*epsilon)+b(1+theta*epsilon), with generic occurrence-wise theta values satisfying |theta| <= 1. Evidence: PDF p. 2, printed p. 758, anchor "equation (3.1)".
[Explicit] fl(ab)=ab(1+theta*epsilon), again with |theta| <= 1. Evidence: PDF p. 2, printed p. 758, anchor "equation (3.2)".

[Explicit] If beta is the floating-point base, t is the number of base-beta mantissa digits, and sums use at least t+1 accumulator digits, epsilon=0.5*beta^(1-t) for rounded operations and epsilon=beta^(1-t) for chopped operations. Evidence: PDF p. 2, printed p. 758, anchor "paragraph following (3.2)"; PDF p. 3, printed p. 759, anchor "continuation of the epsilon definition".

[Explicit] If sums are accumulated with only t digits, epsilon=0.5*(1+1/beta)*beta^(1-t) for rounded operations and epsilon=(1+1/beta)*beta^(1-t) for chopped operations. Evidence: PDF p. 3, printed p. 759, anchor "continuation of the epsilon definition".

[Explicit] Trigonometric computation uses absolute rather than relative error: fl(sin(fl(a)))=sin(a)+gamma*theta*epsilon and fl(cos(fl(a)))=cos(a)+gamma*theta*epsilon. Evidence: PDF p. 3, printed p. 759, anchor "absolute sine/cosine error model".

[Explicit] The model is deterministic worst-case: theta is bounded and generally differs between occurrences; no independence, zero-mean, or probabilistic distribution is assumed. Evidence: PDF p. 2, printed p. 758, anchor "paragraph following equations (3.1)-(3.2)".

[Explicit] Coordinate-stage errors are accumulated through the displayed telescoping identity and inequality (4.2), rather than combined statistically. Evidence: PDF p. 8, printed p. 764, anchor "telescoping decomposition and equation (4.2)".

K(N_l,gamma) must retain its dependence on the chosen radix factorization and the exact piecewise alpha constants from Theorem 1. Evidence: PDF p. 3, printed p. 759, anchor "definition of K(N,gamma) and alpha".

contract_plain_english: Fix an m-dimensional complex input array with coordinate lengths N_1,...,N_m, and let Y be the exact unnormalized Fourier transform with positive exponential phase and zero-based indices from equation (4.1). Evidence: PDF p. 7, printed p. 763, anchor "equation (4.1)". Compute it as the nested sequence of one-dimensional floating-point FFTs T_m through T_1. Evidence: PDF p. 8, printed p. 764, anchor "nested computation and rewriting of (4.1)". Under the Wilkinson addition/product model and the absolute sine/cosine model with constants epsilon and gamma, each coordinate FFT contributes its Theorem 1 constant K(N_l,gamma). Evidence: PDF p. 2, printed p. 758, anchor "equations (3.1)-(3.2)"; PDF p. 3, printed p. 759, anchor "absolute sine/cosine model and definition of K(N,gamma)". Assuming the input RMS is represented exactly or differs only by O(epsilon), the relative RMS forward error satisfies [fl(Y)-Y]_RMS/Y_RMS <= epsilon*sum_{l=1}^m K(N_l,gamma)+O(epsilon^2). Evidence: PDF p. 8, printed p. 764, anchor "Theorem 2(a)"; PDF p. 9, printed p. 765, anchor "completion of the proof". The RMS is the normalized Euclidean magnitude over all output entries, K retains the chosen radix factorization and its exact piecewise constants, the higher-order term must remain, and the displayed ratio implicitly requires Y_RMS to be nonzero. Evidence: PDF p. 3, printed p. 759, anchor "definition of K(N,gamma)"; PDF p. 8, printed p. 764, anchor "multidimensional RMS definition and Theorem 2(a)".
